title: Independent audit of pcell-mwall (C:autonomous-heredity): S, I, B, D and H hold; the death statistics are inflated about 2x by a genealogy artefact
summary: Operator-run audit (audit.md): a construction auditor read world.py and ran a matched chim=0 ablation and a neutral-trait twin; a replication auditor re-ran the unchanged world on unused seeds 41 and 43 and at a 1.5x grid (scale=1.5), with the claim's own analysis scripts; a judge checked their disagreements. No death or division rule exists; H holds against the neutral-trait twin (no mature deaths, no yield rise) and the rise is between cells. The claim's 'low-born die more on 4/4 seeds' and 'already low at birth' come from a MINP=20 remnant artefact that also doubles the death count. B is a self-made but passive M layer placed by an adsorption drift; it counts under RUBRIC L3's quasi-equilibrium clause.

verdicts.limitation: The genealogy's MINP=20 criterion counts a shrinking cell's remnant as a new low-ranked cell that dies again: death counts are about 2x too high, and the claim's birth-rank statistics do not survive removing remnants (split-born cells only: pooled p=0.09; low yield is mostly acquired during life). About half the yield rise comes from faster growth of high-yield cells, not deaths. The M layer is passive (no feedback) and its claimed control bm=0 is not matched (chim=0 is). The neutral-trait twin ran on one seed only (Q:pcell-mwall-physical-deaths re-tests on three). On seed 43 the deepest track is itself a low-yield cell, so the same-individuals evidence is one lineage on seed 41 (track 58).
